NER.hook: Has the youngest population on Earth — around half of Niger is under fifteen.
NER.place: Landlocked and mostly Sahara, sitting directly on top of Nigeria. The two names are the mix-up to watch.
NER.borders: French West Africa's internal lines made international in 1960: survey arcs across the Sahara, a Libyan line inherited from Franco-Italian bargains, and the southern edge along Anglo-French treaty lines of 1898–1906 that split Hausa country with Nigeria.

MLI.hook: Timbuktu was a university town when Oxford was new, and its medieval ruler Mansa Musa may have been the richest person who ever lived.
MLI.place: Landlocked across the western Sahel, with the Niger river arcing through its middle.
MLI.borders: French Sudan's administrative outline: ruler lines across the desert toward Algeria and Mauritania, and a scalloped southern edge negotiated around existing chiefdoms — none of it older than the 1890s.

MRT.hook: Runs one of the longest trains in the world — up to 2.5km of iron ore across the desert, with passengers riding on top of the load.
MRT.place: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic, above Senegal and west of Mali.
MRT.borders: French survey lines linking France's West African and North African holdings — including a right-angled bite at the northeast drawn to skirt then-Spanish Sahara; it annexed the southern third of Western Sahara in 1976 and renounced it in 1979.
